title: SPH4U Unit 1 Kinematics practice test pattern
subject: Physics

learning_goals: Interpret position-time, velocity-time, and acceleration-time representations
Calculate displacement, velocity, and acceleration in one and two dimensions
Analyze constant-acceleration motion, free fall, and projectile motion
Use vector components and frames of reference for relative motion
Interpret and evaluate non-uniform-motion lab data

source_files.notes: Primary source for Unit 1 coverage and test timing within the course
Chapter 1 concepts, worked-example forms, and review; PDF page numbering differs from printed page numbering
Observed advanced multipart projectile and relative-motion practice questions
Observed vector-operation diagrams and constant-acceleration vector extrapolation

observed_patterns: The syllabus covers motion graphs, average and instantaneous velocity, equations of motion, non-uniform-motion lab work, two-dimensional vectors, projectile motion, and relative motion before Test #1.
The training pages contain diagram-based vector tasks and multipart word problems involving projectiles, moving targets, wind, and river current.
The user specifies 15 multiple-choice questions, 5 true/false questions, one 10-mark lab-style question, and three 10-mark application questions.
The user requests approximately equal normal, medium-hard, and hard difficulty in the first paper.
inferred_patterns: Hard items should combine vector components with time, relative velocity, or two-dimensional projectile motion.
A lab item should require interpreting measured motion data rather than only recalling a definition.
The selected-response sections can check sign, direction, graph area/slope, and frame-of-reference misconceptions.
analysis_summary.notes: The supplied images are training questions, not a complete sample test with a verified section structure. The syllabus lesson numbering differs from the supplied Nelson PDF; coverage follows named topics and assigned printed pages. One mark per multiple-choice and true/false item is an explicit generation assumption, giving 60 total marks. Difficulty is balanced by marks: 20 easy, 20 medium, 20 hard.

sections.title: Multiple Choice
sections.instructions: Choose one answer per question; 1 mark each.

sections.title: True or False
sections.instructions: Mark each statement true or false; 1 mark each.

sections.title: Lab Analysis
sections.instructions: Show calculations and interpret the data.

sections.title: Applications
sections.instructions: Show diagrams, equations, units, and directions where applicable.

ordering_rules: Use question numbers 1-24 in section order.
Place 15 multiple choice, then 5 true/false, then one lab item, then three application items.

topic_distribution.topic: Motion quantities, graphs, and one-dimensional kinematics
Vectors and two-dimensional change in velocity

progression_notes: Balance difficulty by marks rather than question count.
The 60-mark paper assigns 20 marks to each level; difficulty increases within each selected-response section and across the applications.

response_formats: worked numerical answer with units and direction
question_style.wording_tone: Clear SPH4U practice-test wording with demanding but unambiguous multi-step applications.
diagram_expectations: Use a vector sketch or labelled axes for two-dimensional applications.
Use graph axes and units for lab data.
answer_style_expectations: Show component equations and sign convention.
Report sensible significant figures and direction.
State assumptions such as negligible air resistance when needed.

trap_patterns.description: Distinguish distance from displacement and speed from velocity.
Distinguish slope from area and signed displacement from total distance.
Maintain a consistent axis convention for velocity change, gravity, and vector bearings.
Add or subtract velocity components in the correct observer frame.
Use a common flight time while keeping horizontal and vertical equations independent.

generation_rules.variation_policy: Keep the assessed skills and multipart reasoning style; change contexts, values, and wording from source practice pages.
freshness_requirements: Use original lab data and application scenarios.
constraints: 20 marks easy, 20 marks medium, 20 marks hard
Cover syllabus Unit 1 named topics and Nelson Chapter 1 content

memory_metadata.summary_for_retrieval: SPH4U Unit 1: 15 MC, 5 T/F, 10-mark lab, three 10-mark applications; 60 marks split equally by difficulty. Coverage: graphs, 1D/2D kinematics, projectiles, relative motion. Hard style combines components and moving frames.

notation_rules: State east and north as positive axes when using components.
Use [angle N of E] or [angle E of N] consistently.
lab_skills: estimate instantaneous velocity with symmetric interval
topic_specific_constraints: Neglect air resistance only when stated.
Keep the syllabus named topics as the scope despite numbering differences with the supplied Nelson PDF.
